# Leonida ## Independent continuation [LeonidaReforge](https://github.com/LeonidaReforge) owns this repository, and [@JokerDreamerCoder](https://github.com/JokerDreamerCoder) is its maintainer. This is an independent continuation of the original open-source Leonida project. Thank you to its original developers, researchers, maintainers, and contributors. The recovered Git history retains their authorship, and existing license and copyright notices still apply. LeonidaReforge is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or acting on behalf of Rockstar Games, Take-Two Interactive, Microsoft, or the project's former administration. Historical links and measurements are credited to the original project; they are not verification by LeonidaReforge. Leonida is an experimental build-it-yourself project aiming to run the Xbox Series version of Grand Theft Auto VI on Windows from a user's own copy. It does not provide a playable release.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Governance

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. ## Project status The table is an inherited snapshot of the original project's work, not a current compatibility report. LeonidaReforge has not independently reproduced these historical results. The continuation does not claim a verified retail boot or working gameplay. | What | Status | |---|---| | Booting, story mode, anything playable | ❌ No | | Finding and checking your copy (Xbox Series 1.0.2.1) | ✅ Works | | Shaders: carve, unpack native RDNA2 code, disassemble | ✅ All 26,503 | | Shaders: RDNA2 → SPIR-V translation | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 translated**: 2,236 VS, 12,101 PS, 2,689 CS, 9,282 mesh, 195 geometry, with a per-shader metadata index for pipeline creation. The LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and the LLVM 23.1.3 Windows rerun at `43d0015` both translated all 26,503 ([Linux](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [Windows](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7074299915)). Translation and SPIR-V validation are separate steps; validation results are listed below. ⚠️ 23,841 are wave64: exact on 64-wide subgroups (AMD). On 32-wide subgroups (NVIDIA, Intel), compute and mesh shaders are exact with wave64 emulation (`--wave64-emulate`, on by default there); cross-half wave ops in vertex, pixel and geometry shaders are still approximate | | SPIR-V validation (`spirv-val`) | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 passed** in the LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and in the full-corpus rerun at `43d4703`, after `dcd8ecf` fixed the SPIR-V ID-bound error ([Linux rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [full-corpus rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/881#issuecomment-7075507328)). On Windows at `43d0015`, all 26,503 translated but 26,501 passed validation; the two ID-bound failures were fixed by `dcd8ecf`. The intermediate `dedd75c` run also passed 26,501. | | Shader translator checked on a real GPU | ⚠️ The hand-written GPU tests (vertex fetch, texture sampling, exports, ALU ops, partial-register ops, barycentrics, wave-uniform branches, compute LDS/barriers/buffer stores, wave64 masks) have been run on more than 30 GPU and driver combinations, with results in [#166](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/166): NVIDIA Turing, Ampere, Ada and Blackwell (Windows and Linux); AMD GCN3, RDNA1, RDNA2, RDNA3 and RDNA4 (Windows driver and RADV); Intel Gen9 (ANV); Apple M1 (MoltenVK, no geometry or mesh stages); and Mesa llvmpipe. Wave64 tests need 64-wide subgroups (AMD) or `LEONIDA_W64_EMULATE=1`. These are small test shaders: the game's own shaders are checked by `spirv-val` and by driver pipeline creation (`vk_pipeline_check`), not by their output | | Models (OBJ with real names, UVs, material references) | ✅ Exported. A ten-archive scan at decoder pin `e293917` recovered **382,781 models** with zero readback decode failures. This includes **343,327** models from `levels.rpf`. A full OBJ export of that archive is pending. See [recount and export scope](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). | | Texture dictionaries and world texture pools (DDS) | ✅ Exported. `rpf9dump` decodes BCPack BC1, BC3, BC4 and BC5 chunks in strict mode and skips BC6H, BC7 and chunks that need unconfirmed history; the assets stage then completes what it can with a clean-room decoder (`tools/bcpack.py`, which `tools/ttpf_assets.py` runs through `tools/ttpf_mips.py`) that rebuilds BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7, and records the rest as a `BCPackLimitation` in `manifest.json` (most BC6H/BC7 chunks and the unconfirmed-history ones need a local history table, which the repo does not ship) ([notes](docs/textures.md)) | | Audio banks (AWC: Opus, XMA2) | ✅ Exported whole. Opus repackaged **losslessly** as Ogg Opus; PCM (codec 0/2) as WAV; XMA2 decoded with ffmpeg. `--wav` adds 16-bit PCM WAV ([notes](docs/audio.md)) | | Music/radio config | ? Measured. **1,589** audio-config records with exact durations and AWC stream ids; station grouping and content-id lists; no per-track start offsets ([notes](docs/audio_config.md)) | | PE loader and import shims | ⚠️ Runs a stand-in executable end to end (`gta6rt --run`: CRT startup, statics, heap, files, threads, GDK imports through the shims, exit code back). Controllers through a GameInput shim on SDL3 (any controller SDL supports, rumble, DualSense trigger effects and lightbar; built when SDL3 is installed or with `-DLEONIDA_SDL3_FETCH=ON`, [notes](docs/gameinput.md)). `--trace-d3d12` logs every D3D12 call and its outcome for the first boot. Untested against the real executable | | Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan | ⚠️ In progress. A Vulkan-backed device behind the Xbox-ABI proxy creates queues, command lists, fences, descriptor heaps, committed, placed and reserved resources, render-target and depth views (3D targets included), texture views and samplers (2D, cube, 1D and 3D views, the depth and stencil planes of depth-stencil textures, packed formats such as B5G6R5, B4G4R4A4 and R9G9B9E5, buffer SRVs — raw, structured and typed; they go into the bindless set), root signatures, pipelines and query heaps, and draws run on Vulkan. Barriers, clears, uploads, copies (BC included), colour resolves, predication, CPU-side texture reads and writes, and occlusion, timestamp and pipeline-statistics queries run on Vulkan, checked on one GPU. The console-shaped command-list proxy, the measured `PresentX` queue slots (30/32, layout-detected) wired to the presentation core, and `AllocateUploadMemory` (list slot 148, a mapped-upload arena whose addresses translate to buffer device addresses in root descriptors and IA/SO views) cover the console-ABI surface the package measures. Still open: the console list tail and the descriptor-table record model ([plan](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)) | | Ray tracing (BVH) | ⚠️ In progress. `BuildRaytracingAccelerationStructure` builds BLASes and TLASes on the GPU in the console's XDXR BVH4 layout (the default; `LEONIDA_RT_AS=khr` uses Vulkan's own acceleration structures instead), which the translated shaders walk themselves through `image_bvh_intersect_ray` (all four triangle node types, TRI0-TRI3, with the barycentric remap byte); the GPU builder writes TRI0 and TRI1 leaves. Updates refit instead of rebuilding, and clone, compaction and the compacted/current postbuild sizes work; checked against a CPU reference on synthetic scenes. The build descriptions are recovered from the package's `XboxBvhBuilder.dll` ([notes](docs/xdxr.md)). The game's `*_bvh4.rpf` packs are measured: offline-built, dehydrated BLASes that rehydrate through that DLL with their geometry from the drawables in `levels.rpf` (measured on 8 of the 10 sampled BLAS; [notes](docs/bvh.md)). Not done in the builder: serialization. TRI1 pairing (no memory saved yet) and BOX16 nodes for `MINIMIZE_MEMORY` BLASes (an assumed switch) are in ([notes](docs/bvh.md)). Open: whether the game rehydrates the packs or rebuilds them ([#313](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/313)) | The table above is written by hand. To measure it on your own checkout (unit and runtime tests, which rows of the translator contract were confirmed on a GPU, measured imports, your corpus counts and, with `--github`, CI and the `D3D-` items), run `python -I tools/progress_dashboard.py --out ` and open `progress.html` ([notes](docs/progress_dashboard.md)). ## Platforms The following platform notes describe historical test coverage, not a current playability claim: | Platform | Historical coverage | |---|---| | Windows | Everything: `make_game.py`, the tools, and the runtime (`gta6rt` and the D3D12 → Vulkan layer) with its tests. | | Linux | The translator, the asset tools and the Vulkan GPU test tools build and run natively (tested on RADV and NVIDIA). The runtime is Windows code: it cross-compiles with clang-cl and xwin, and its tests run under Wine or Proton (*The Windows runtime on Linux, under Wine or Proton* below). The game is meant to run the same way, under Wine or Proton with the D3D12 layer on native Vulkan (#217). | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | The Python tools and the Vulkan test tools run natively, on MoltenVK (Homebrew) or KosmicKrisp. The runtime is Windows code and runs as on Linux, under Wine: CrossOver, arm64 with FEX or x86-64 under Rosetta (#1706, #1707, #1924; #3119 fixes the last loader tests there). Known gaps: no geometry stage and no `VK_EXT_mesh_shader` (those tests are skipped), 32-wide subgroups (wave64 shaders run emulated), and MoltenVK's float handling (`PerVertexKHR`, NaN compares, -0, the cost of `NoContraction`); [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) lists each (#2947). | | AMD RDNA1 (RX 5000) | A supported target: close to the console's RDNA2, and its 64-wide subgroups run the wave64 shaders natively. RX 5700 XT results pass the GPU test suite (#146); on RADV, pixel shaders without fragment barycentrics have a known difference (*Known problems* in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)) (#330). | See [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) to run and report new GPU tests. The original issue #166 is a historical reference. ## How to build The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy. **The easy way:** 1. Install the prerequisites below. 2. Download this project **with its submodule**: `git clone --recursive https://github.com/LeonidaReforge/Leonida.git`. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out `third_party/rpf9-explorer`. The build fetches it if `git` is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do. 3. Double-click **`Build.bat`**. It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to `Documents\Leonida`. A stopped build continues where it left off. Your game folder is the one that holds `MicrosoftGame.Config` and the `.rpf` archives, as plain files. **Prerequisites:** - **Your own copy** of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1. - **Windows 10/11 x64**, with about **400 GB** free for work files (an assets export alone measured about 337 GB before its audio step, in about 2 h 35 min). Disk sizes here are as Windows Explorer shows them, which are GiB: 400 GiB is about 430 GB in decimal units. They can go on another drive with `--work`. - [Python 3.12+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (tick "Add python.exe to PATH"). - [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0). - [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/), for `spirv-as` / `spirv-val`. - [LLVM 21+](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases) with the **AMDGPU target** for `llvm-mc`. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, `scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1` builds a native `llvm-mc.exe` with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets `LLVM_MC`; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use [conda](https://docs.conda.io/): `conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools` (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) used version 23.1.6), then set `LLVM_MC` to the full path of the `llvm-mc.exe` it installs (`where.exe llvm-mc` shows it once the environment is active; in PowerShell a bare `where` is `Where-Object`). Or install `llvm-21` in WSL and set `LLVM_MC` to the whole command, `LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc"` (see [docs/design.md](docs/design.md#disassembling-shaders)). On Linux, `llvm-mc` on PATH is enough. - Visual Studio 2022 with **Desktop development with C++** and the **Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer**, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare). - [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for `--wav`). **Low disk space:** the ~400 GB figure is for the full build. To *run* the port, `--stages check,shaders,runtime` needs about 30 GB; the `assets` stage (~370 GB) is only for the asset tools, and `--wav` adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). `--work` and `--out` can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs `gta6rt --overlay `; `--overlay` is a `gta6rt` option, not a `make_game.py` one. Leave the `.s` files in `work/shaders/dxbc/disasm` in place: the next run checks them against the list in `disasm.done` and disassembles the missing ones again (all of them for a folder whose `disasm.done` predates that list), then translates every shader again. A `disasm` folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it. **From a terminal**, with the same behaviour and more control: ```powershell python -I make_game.py --find # list the copies found on this PC python -I make_game.py --pick # choose the game folder in a folder dialog python -I make_game.py --check # check your copy, build nothing python -I make_game.py --check --full-check # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow) python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work" python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets # only some stages python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large) python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off # auto (default), on or off; see below ``` `--wave64-emulate` decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, `auto`, asks `vulkaninfo` (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With `--mesh-compute`, only compute subgroup support is needed. On AMD's Windows driver, `auto` uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or `vulkaninfo` is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support. The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. `auto` can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use `--wave64-emulate on` to force emulation or `--wave64-emulate off` to force native wave64. Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: `--no-float-controls` (drop `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve`, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without `shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32`; needs PR #664's translator flag), `--bary-fallback` (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`), `--texel-offset-fallback` (fold `image_sample*_o` offsets into the coordinate, for devices without `VK_KHR_maintenance8`) and `--mesh-compute` (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`; on by itself on Intel's Windows Vulkan driver, whose native mesh draws crash, BUILD-2202, unless `--native-mesh`). Each is documented in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs. The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information. The build also records which decoder (the `third_party/rpf9-explorer` commit and the `tools/rpf9dump` sources) exported each archive's models and textures and each texture pool. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models, textures and pools are exported once more after upgrading. Stages: `check` always runs first; then `shaders`, `assets` and `runtime` run together when selected (they do not depend on each other). `pipelines` starts once the translated shaders are ready and, when this run includes runtime, that stage has finished rebuilding `vk_pipeline_check`, so it can overlap the rest of assets; it creates every translated shader on your GPU driver, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to `pipeline_cache.bin` in `--out` (the runtime doesn't load that cache yet, so it doesn't speed up the first boot). The shader translation is the longest CPU step: it runs on `--jobs` processes (half the CPU threads by default). When shaders and assets share the machine, that budget is split between them and passed to `rpf9dump` as `--jobs`; a solo assets run still lets `rpf9dump` use every core. Progress lines include percent and a rough ETA for translation shards, asset steps, and overall stage completion. On an interactive terminal, a LEONIDA setup screen lets you set jobs and whether stages overlap, then a key-switchable per-stage log view (`1`–`4` / `Tab`) keeps parallel output demuxed; full stage logs go under `work/logs/`. Use `--no-tui` (or redirect stdout) for the plain console. `--wav` is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to `work\assets\audio\wav` after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes. ### Vulkan diagnostics on Linux With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed: ```sh cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel ./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv ``` Pass the directory containing `index.json` and the translated SPIR-V files to `vk_pipeline_check`. `make_game.py` runs on Linux too. The `pipelines` stage uses the `vk_pipeline_check` built above (`runtime/build/linux`, or `runtime/build`), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing. ### Running the loader on Linux The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every push to `main` that changes `runtime/`, and on demand from the Actions tab (the `wine` job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the `runtime` stage cross-builds it into `runtime/build/windows` with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#known-problems); plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as `clang-cl-21`) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin) lays out, in `XWIN_DIR` or `~/.local/share/xwin-sdk` ([docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#the-windows-runtime-on-linux-under-wine-or-proton) has the one-time `xwin` command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the `runtime-windows` artifact of that workflow's `windows` job, unzipped: ```sh python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows ``` Either way it copies `gta6rt.exe` and `gta6rt_tls_host.dll` into `--out` and writes `gta6rt.sh` next to them, which starts `gta6rt.exe` with `wine`, or with the Wine named by `WINE` (for Proton, its `files/bin/wine`). The same option skips the build on Windows. On Linux, run `/gta6rt.sh --dry-run` to inspect the packaged title's imports, then `/gta6rt.sh --init` to check TLS callbacks and DLL initialization. Use `/gta6rt.sh --run` for startup. These commands use the package in `game_path.txt`, the port's `overlay` for writes, and Vulkan by default. When the Vulkan backend is selected with `LEONIDA_D3D12=vulkan`, the packaged runtime finds the translated shaders in `/shaders/spirv` using `shader_path.txt` beside `gta6rt.exe`. Set `LEONIDA_SHADERS` to use another directory. ## How it works | Piece | What it does | Where | |---|---|---| | Version check | Every package file's name, size and SHA-256 for each supported version | `game/`, `make_game.py` | | Shader pipeline | Carves DXBC containers from `shaders.rpf` without its encrypted table of contents. Unpacks the `XBCH` → `FSSM` native RDNA2 program, disassembles it with LLVM (`gfx1013`) and translates it to SPIR-V | `tools/shader_carve.py` ([optional Rust scanner](tools/shader_carve_native/README.md)), `fssm_unpack.py`, `shader_disasm.py`, `rdna2spirv.py` | | Asset export | Finds validated resources inside RPF9 archives and the loose `.ttpf` texture pools | `tools/rpf9dump` (on rpf9-explorer's Core) | | Runtime | Maps the PE image, resolves imports to shims (GDK, XMem, `d3d12_xs`) | `runtime/` | | Research tools | PE/RTTI inspection, raw carving, texture tiling probes, GPU test harnesses | `tools/`, `runtime/test/` | | Progress dashboard | One offline page of what passes, what changed since it last passed and what blocks next, built from test results and the docs' own tables; nothing is written inside the repo | `tools/progress_dashboard.py` | The translator's runtime contract (user SGPRs, push constants, memory model, bindless images, vertex fetch, system values) and all the format notes are in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md); the format, asset, runtime and validation notes are indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). The Xbox D3D12 plan is in [docs/d3d12_vulkan.md](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md). Audio bank formats and the export tools are in [docs/audio.md](docs/audio.md); [docs/related_projects.md](docs/related_projects.md) records the prior art we may read and the licence limits on it. ## Want to help? The biggest open pieces: - **Shader translator on hardware**: compute, mesh and geometry now translate (see the translator contract in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)); still open are the vertex-shader input layout (`v0` = `VertexIndex` is unverified if the console runs VS as NGG) and wave64 cross-half code in VS/PS/GS on 32-wide subgroups. - **Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan**: see the [technical plan and historical status](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md). Check the new repository's issues and pull requests for current work before starting. - **Model recovery**: investigate the 71 unrecovered fragment candidates in [`levels.rpf`](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), and the [repository issues](https://github.com/LeonidaReforge/Leonida/issues). Never attach game files, extracted assets or generated shaders to issues or pull requests. ## Credits - [rpf9-explorer](https://github.com/breadbbbb/rpf9-explorer) by breadbbbb: the RPF9 model, texture-pool and AWC decoders used by `tools/rpf9dump` (git submodule). - [Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa) (MIT): GFX10 resource-descriptor layout (`tools/gfx10_formats.json`), and the ACO/RADV rules used as reference for 16-bit results and shader system registers. - [libHttpClient](https://github.com/microsoft/libHttpClient) (MIT) by Microsoft: the XTaskQueue/XAsync implementation in `third_party/xtaskqueue`, used by the offline `xgameruntime` shim. - [LLVM](https://llvm.org/): AMDGPU disassembler. - Historical logo credit: ["Grand Theft Auto VI" icon by SlyDevil](https://www.steamgriddb.com/icon/122618) on SteamGridDB. The inherited artwork is not used in the current tree; see the [redistribution review](docs/redistribution-review.md). - [SPIRV-Tools](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Tools): assembly and validation. Grand Theft Auto and all related names are trademarks of their owners. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by them. ## License GPLv3 (or any later version). See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party code keeps its own license.

Leonida

Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. Discord: https://discord.gg/xsqS3DqqVF Custom Git Mirror: https://git.notrexed.dev/notrexed/Leonida
## Project status **Early. The game does not boot yet.** Everything that can be done without the game's executable is in place, so work on booting can start as soon as one is available to a developer. | What | Status | |---|---| | Booting, story mode, anything playable | ❌ No | | Finding and checking your copy (Xbox Series 1.0.2.1) | ✅ Works | | Shaders: carve, unpack native RDNA2 code, disassemble | ✅ All 26,503 | | Shaders: RDNA2 → SPIR-V translation | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 translated**: 2,236 VS, 12,101 PS, 2,689 CS, 9,282 mesh, 195 geometry, with a per-shader metadata index for pipeline creation. The LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and the LLVM 23.1.3 Windows rerun at `43d0015` both translated all 26,503 ([Linux](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [Windows](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7074299915)). Translation and SPIR-V validation are separate steps; validation results are listed below. ⚠️ 23,841 are wave64: exact on 64-wide subgroups (AMD). On 32-wide subgroups (NVIDIA, Intel), compute and mesh shaders are exact with wave64 emulation (`--wave64-emulate`, on by default there); cross-half wave ops in vertex, pixel and geometry shaders are still approximate | | SPIR-V validation (`spirv-val`) | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 passed** in the LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and in the full-corpus rerun at `43d4703`, after `dcd8ecf` fixed the SPIR-V ID-bound error ([Linux rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [full-corpus rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/881#issuecomment-7075507328)). On Windows at `43d0015`, all 26,503 translated but 26,501 passed validation; the two ID-bound failures were fixed by `dcd8ecf`. The intermediate `dedd75c` run also passed 26,501. | | Shader translator checked on a real GPU | ⚠️ The hand-written GPU tests (vertex fetch, texture sampling, exports, ALU ops, partial-register ops, barycentrics, wave-uniform branches, compute LDS/barriers/buffer stores, wave64 masks) have been run on more than 30 GPU and driver combinations, with results in [#166](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/166): NVIDIA Turing, Ampere, Ada and Blackwell (Windows and Linux); AMD GCN3, RDNA1, RDNA2, RDNA3 and RDNA4 (Windows driver and RADV); Intel Gen9 (ANV); Apple M1 (MoltenVK, no geometry or mesh stages); and Mesa llvmpipe. Wave64 tests need 64-wide subgroups (AMD) or `LEONIDA_W64_EMULATE=1`. These are small test shaders: the game's own shaders are checked by `spirv-val` and by driver pipeline creation (`vk_pipeline_check`), not by their output | | Models (OBJ with real names, UVs, material references) | ✅ Exported. A ten-archive scan at decoder pin `e293917` recovered **382,781 models** with zero readback decode failures. This includes **343,327** models from `levels.rpf`. A full OBJ export of that archive is pending. See [recount and export scope](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). | | Texture dictionaries and world texture pools (DDS) | ✅ Exported. `rpf9dump` decodes BCPack BC1, BC3, BC4 and BC5 chunks in strict mode and skips BC6H, BC7 and chunks that need unconfirmed history; the assets stage then completes what it can with a clean-room decoder (`tools/bcpack.py`, which `tools/ttpf_assets.py` runs through `tools/ttpf_mips.py`) that rebuilds BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7, and records the rest as a `BCPackLimitation` in `manifest.json` (most BC6H/BC7 chunks and the unconfirmed-history ones need a local history table, which the repo does not ship) ([notes](docs/textures.md)) | | Audio banks (AWC: Opus, XMA2) | ✅ Exported whole. Opus repackaged **losslessly** as Ogg Opus; PCM (codec 0/2) as WAV; XMA2 decoded with ffmpeg. `--wav` adds 16-bit PCM WAV ([notes](docs/audio.md)) | | Music/radio config | ? Measured. **1,589** audio-config records with exact durations and AWC stream ids; station grouping and content-id lists; no per-track start offsets ([notes](docs/audio_config.md)) | | PE loader and import shims | ⚠️ Runs a stand-in executable end to end (`gta6rt --run`: CRT startup, statics, heap, files, threads, GDK imports through the shims, exit code back). Controllers through a GameInput shim on SDL3 (any controller SDL supports, rumble, DualSense trigger effects and lightbar; built when SDL3 is installed or with `-DLEONIDA_SDL3_FETCH=ON`, [notes](docs/gameinput.md)). `--trace-d3d12` logs every D3D12 call and its outcome for the first boot. Untested against the real executable | | Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan | ⚠️ In progress. A Vulkan-backed device behind the Xbox-ABI proxy creates queues, command lists, fences, descriptor heaps, committed, placed and reserved resources, render-target and depth views (3D targets included), texture views and samplers (2D, cube, 1D and 3D views, the depth and stencil planes of depth-stencil textures, packed formats such as B5G6R5, B4G4R4A4 and R9G9B9E5, buffer SRVs — raw, structured and typed; they go into the bindless set), root signatures, pipelines and query heaps, and draws run on Vulkan. Barriers, clears, uploads, copies (BC included), colour resolves, predication, CPU-side texture reads and writes, and occlusion, timestamp and pipeline-statistics queries run on Vulkan, checked on one GPU. The console-shaped command-list proxy, the measured `PresentX` queue slots (30/32, layout-detected) wired to the presentation core, and `AllocateUploadMemory` (list slot 148, a mapped-upload arena whose addresses translate to buffer device addresses in root descriptors and IA/SO views) cover the console-ABI surface the package measures. Still open: the console list tail and the descriptor-table record model ([plan](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)) | | Ray tracing (BVH) | ⚠️ In progress. `BuildRaytracingAccelerationStructure` builds BLASes and TLASes on the GPU in the console's XDXR BVH4 layout (the default; `LEONIDA_RT_AS=khr` uses Vulkan's own acceleration structures instead), which the translated shaders walk themselves through `image_bvh_intersect_ray` (all four triangle node types, TRI0-TRI3, with the barycentric remap byte); the GPU builder writes TRI0 and TRI1 leaves. Updates refit instead of rebuilding, and clone, compaction and the compacted/current postbuild sizes work; checked against a CPU reference on synthetic scenes. The build descriptions are recovered from the package's `XboxBvhBuilder.dll` ([notes](docs/xdxr.md)). The game's `*_bvh4.rpf` packs are measured: offline-built, dehydrated BLASes that rehydrate through that DLL with their geometry from the drawables in `levels.rpf` (measured on 8 of the 10 sampled BLAS; [notes](docs/bvh.md)). Not done in the builder: serialization. TRI1 pairing (no memory saved yet) and BOX16 nodes for `MINIMIZE_MEMORY` BLASes (an assumed switch) are in ([notes](docs/bvh.md)). Open: whether the game rehydrates the packs or rebuilds them ([#313](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/313)) | The table above is written by hand. To measure it on your own checkout (unit and runtime tests, which rows of the translator contract were confirmed on a GPU, measured imports, your corpus counts and, with `--github`, CI and the `D3D-` items), run `python -I tools/progress_dashboard.py --out ` and open `progress.html` ([notes](docs/progress_dashboard.md)). ## Platforms Nothing is playable on any platform yet (see *Project status*). What runs where today: | Platform | Today | |---|---| | Windows | Everything: `make_game.py`, the tools, and the runtime (`gta6rt` and the D3D12 → Vulkan layer) with its tests. | | Linux | The translator, the asset tools and the Vulkan GPU test tools build and run natively (tested on RADV and NVIDIA). The runtime is Windows code: it cross-compiles with clang-cl and xwin, and its tests run under Wine or Proton (*The Windows runtime on Linux, under Wine or Proton* below). The game is meant to run the same way, under Wine or Proton with the D3D12 layer on native Vulkan (#217). | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | The Python tools and the Vulkan test tools run natively, on MoltenVK (Homebrew) or KosmicKrisp. The runtime is Windows code and runs as on Linux, under Wine: CrossOver, arm64 with FEX or x86-64 under Rosetta (#1706, #1707, #1924; #3119 fixes the last loader tests there). Known gaps: no geometry stage and no `VK_EXT_mesh_shader` (those tests are skipped), 32-wide subgroups (wave64 shaders run emulated), and MoltenVK's float handling (`PerVertexKHR`, NaN compares, -0, the cost of `NoContraction`); [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) lists each (#2947). | | AMD RDNA1 (RX 5000) | A supported target: close to the console's RDNA2, and its 64-wide subgroups run the wave64 shaders natively. RX 5700 XT results pass the GPU test suite (#146); on RADV, pixel shaders without fragment barycentrics have a known difference (*Known problems* in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)) (#330). | GPU results from every platform are collected in #166; how to run the tests is in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). ## How to build The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy. **The easy way:** 1. Install the prerequisites below. 2. Download this project **with its submodule**: `git clone --recursive https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida`. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out `third_party/rpf9-explorer`. The build fetches it if `git` is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do. 3. Double-click **`Build.bat`**. It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to `Documents\Leonida`. A stopped build continues where it left off. Your game folder is the one that holds `MicrosoftGame.Config` and the `.rpf` archives, as plain files. **Prerequisites:** - **Your own copy** of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1. - **Windows 10/11 x64**, with about **400 GB** free for work files (an assets export alone measured about 337 GB before its audio step, in about 2 h 35 min). Disk sizes here are as Windows Explorer shows them, which are GiB: 400 GiB is about 430 GB in decimal units. They can go on another drive with `--work`. - [Python 3.12+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (tick "Add python.exe to PATH"). - [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0). - [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/), for `spirv-as` / `spirv-val`. - [LLVM 21+](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases) with the **AMDGPU target** for `llvm-mc`. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, `scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1` builds a native `llvm-mc.exe` with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets `LLVM_MC`; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use [conda](https://docs.conda.io/): `conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools` (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) used version 23.1.6), then set `LLVM_MC` to the full path of the `llvm-mc.exe` it installs (`where.exe llvm-mc` shows it once the environment is active; in PowerShell a bare `where` is `Where-Object`). Or install `llvm-21` in WSL and set `LLVM_MC` to the whole command, `LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc"` (see [docs/design.md](docs/design.md#disassembling-shaders)). On Linux, `llvm-mc` on PATH is enough. - Visual Studio 2022 with **Desktop development with C++** and the **Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer**, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare). - [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for `--wav`). **Is this PC strong enough?** [Can I Run Leonida](https://assttro.github.io/can-i-run-leonida/) is a lightweight browser-based checker that compares your PC against reference profiles. It's a rough estimate, not a benchmark. **Low disk space:** the ~400 GB figure is for the full build. To *run* the port, `--stages check,shaders,runtime` needs about 30 GB; the `assets` stage (~370 GB) is only for the asset tools, and `--wav` adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). `--work` and `--out` can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs `gta6rt --overlay `; `--overlay` is a `gta6rt` option, not a `make_game.py` one. Leave the `.s` files in `work/shaders/dxbc/disasm` in place: the next run checks them against the list in `disasm.done` and disassembles the missing ones again (all of them for a folder whose `disasm.done` predates that list), then translates every shader again. A `disasm` folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it. **From a terminal**, with the same behaviour and more control: ```powershell python -I make_game.py --find # list the copies found on this PC python -I make_game.py --pick # choose the game folder in a folder dialog python -I make_game.py --check # check your copy, build nothing python -I make_game.py --check --full-check # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow) python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work" python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets # only some stages python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large) python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off # auto (default), on or off; see below ``` `--wave64-emulate` decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, `auto`, asks `vulkaninfo` (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With `--mesh-compute`, only compute subgroup support is needed. On AMD's Windows driver, `auto` uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or `vulkaninfo` is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support. The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. `auto` can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use `--wave64-emulate on` to force emulation or `--wave64-emulate off` to force native wave64. Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: `--no-float-controls` (drop `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve`, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without `shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32`; needs PR #664's translator flag), `--bary-fallback` (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`), `--texel-offset-fallback` (fold `image_sample*_o` offsets into the coordinate, for devices without `VK_KHR_maintenance8`) and `--mesh-compute` (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`; on by itself on Intel's Windows Vulkan driver, whose native mesh draws crash, BUILD-2202, unless `--native-mesh`). Each is documented in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs. The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information. The build also records which decoder (the `third_party/rpf9-explorer` commit and the `tools/rpf9dump` sources) exported each archive's models and textures and each texture pool. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models, textures and pools are exported once more after upgrading. Stages: `check` always runs first; then `shaders`, `assets` and `runtime` run together when selected (they do not depend on each other). `pipelines` starts once the translated shaders are ready and, when this run includes runtime, that stage has finished rebuilding `vk_pipeline_check`, so it can overlap the rest of assets; it creates every translated shader on your GPU driver, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to `pipeline_cache.bin` in `--out` (the runtime doesn't load that cache yet, so it doesn't speed up the first boot). The shader translation is the longest CPU step: it runs on `--jobs` processes (half the CPU threads by default). When shaders and assets share the machine, that budget is split between them and passed to `rpf9dump` as `--jobs`; a solo assets run still lets `rpf9dump` use every core. Progress lines include percent and a rough ETA for translation shards, asset steps, and overall stage completion. On an interactive terminal, a LEONIDA setup screen lets you set jobs and whether stages overlap, then a key-switchable per-stage log view (`1`–`4` / `Tab`) keeps parallel output demuxed; full stage logs go under `work/logs/`. Use `--no-tui` (or redirect stdout) for the plain console. `--wav` is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to `work\assets\audio\wav` after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes. ### Vulkan diagnostics on Linux With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed: ```sh cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel ./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv ``` Pass the directory containing `index.json` and the translated SPIR-V files to `vk_pipeline_check`. `make_game.py` runs on Linux too. The `pipelines` stage uses the `vk_pipeline_check` built above (`runtime/build/linux`, or `runtime/build`), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing. ### Running the loader on Linux The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every push to `main` that changes `runtime/`, and on demand from the Actions tab (the `wine` job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the `runtime` stage cross-builds it into `runtime/build/windows` with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#known-problems); plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as `clang-cl-21`) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin) lays out, in `XWIN_DIR` or `~/.local/share/xwin-sdk` ([docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#the-windows-runtime-on-linux-under-wine-or-proton) has the one-time `xwin` command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the `runtime-windows` artifact of that workflow's `windows` job, unzipped: ```sh python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows ``` Either way it copies `gta6rt.exe` and `gta6rt_tls_host.dll` into `--out` and writes `gta6rt.sh` next to them, which starts `gta6rt.exe` with `wine`, or with the Wine named by `WINE` (for Proton, its `files/bin/wine`). The same option skips the build on Windows. On Linux, run `/gta6rt.sh --dry-run` to inspect the packaged title's imports, then `/gta6rt.sh --init` to check TLS callbacks and DLL initialization. Use `/gta6rt.sh --run` for startup. These commands use the package in `game_path.txt`, the port's `overlay` for writes, and Vulkan by default. When the Vulkan backend is selected with `LEONIDA_D3D12=vulkan`, the packaged runtime finds the translated shaders in `/shaders/spirv` using `shader_path.txt` beside `gta6rt.exe`. Set `LEONIDA_SHADERS` to use another directory. ## How it works | Piece | What it does | Where | |---|---|---| | Version check | Every package file's name, size and SHA-256 for each supported version | `game/`, `make_game.py` | | Shader pipeline | Carves DXBC containers from `shaders.rpf` without its encrypted table of contents. Unpacks the `XBCH` → `FSSM` native RDNA2 program, disassembles it with LLVM (`gfx1013`) and translates it to SPIR-V | `tools/shader_carve.py` ([optional Rust scanner](tools/shader_carve_native/README.md)), `fssm_unpack.py`, `shader_disasm.py`, `rdna2spirv.py` | | Asset export | Finds validated resources inside RPF9 archives and the loose `.ttpf` texture pools | `tools/rpf9dump` (on rpf9-explorer's Core) | | Runtime | Maps the PE image, resolves imports to shims (GDK, XMem, `d3d12_xs`) | `runtime/` | | Research tools | PE/RTTI inspection, raw carving, texture tiling probes, GPU test harnesses | `tools/`, `runtime/test/` | | Progress dashboard | One offline page of what passes, what changed since it last passed and what blocks next, built from test results and the docs' own tables; nothing is written inside the repo | `tools/progress_dashboard.py` | The translator's runtime contract (user SGPRs, push constants, memory model, bindless images, vertex fetch, system values) and all the format notes are in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md); the format, asset, runtime and validation notes are indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). The Xbox D3D12 plan is in [docs/d3d12_vulkan.md](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md). Audio bank formats and the export tools are in [docs/audio.md](docs/audio.md); [docs/related_projects.md](docs/related_projects.md) records the prior art we may read and the licence limits on it. ## Want to help? The biggest open pieces: - **Shader translator on hardware**: compute, mesh and geometry now translate (see the translator contract in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)); still open are the vertex-shader input layout (`v0` = `VertexIndex` is unverified if the console runs VS as NGG) and wave64 cross-half code in VS/PS/GS on 32-wide subgroups. - **Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan**: mesh-shader draws, indirect draw state and stream output are still open; #313 tracks the remaining method surface, and nothing has been checked against the real executable yet ([plan and status](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)). - **Model recovery**: investigate the 71 unrecovered fragment candidates in [`levels.rpf`](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Never attach game files, extracted assets or generated shaders to issues or pull requests. ## Credits - [rpf9-explorer](https://github.com/breadbbbb/rpf9-explorer) by breadbbbb: the RPF9 model, texture-pool and AWC decoders used by `tools/rpf9dump` (git submodule). - [Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa) (MIT): GFX10 resource-descriptor layout (`tools/gfx10_formats.json`), and the ACO/RADV rules used as reference for 16-bit results and shader system registers. - [libHttpClient](https://github.com/microsoft/libHttpClient) (MIT) by Microsoft: the XTaskQueue/XAsync implementation in `third_party/xtaskqueue`, used by the offline `xgameruntime` shim. - [LLVM](https://llvm.org/): AMDGPU disassembler. - Logo: ["Grand Theft Auto VI" icon by SlyDevil](https://www.steamgriddb.com/icon/122618) on SteamGridDB. - [SPIRV-Tools](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Tools): assembly and validation. Leonida

Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. Discord: https://discord.gg/mjgjRFcUWW Custom Git Mirror: https://git.notrexed.dev/notrexed/Leonida

On 32-wide subgroups (NVIDIA, Intel), compute and mesh shaders are exact with wave64 emulation (`--wave64-emulate`, on by default there); cross-half wave ops in vertex, pixel and geometry shaders are still approximate | | SPIR-V validation (`spirv-val`) | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 passed** in the LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and in the full-corpus rerun at `43d4703`, after `dcd8ecf` fixed the SPIR-V ID-bound error ([Linux rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [full-corpus rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/881#issuecomment-7075507328)). On Windows at `43d0015`, all 26,503 translated but 26,501 passed validation; the two ID-bound failures were fixed by `dcd8ecf`. The intermediate `dedd75c` run also passed 26,501. | | Shader translator checked on a real GPU | ⚠️ The hand-written GPU tests (vertex fetch, texture sampling, exports, ALU ops, partial-register ops, barycentrics, wave-uniform branches, compute LDS/barriers/buffer stores, wave64 masks) have been run on more than 30 GPU and driver combinations, with results in [#166](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/166): NVIDIA Turing, Ampere, Ada and Blackwell (Windows and Linux); AMD GCN3, RDNA1, RDNA2, RDNA3 and RDNA4 (Windows driver and RADV); Intel Gen9 (ANV); Apple M1 (MoltenVK, no geometry or mesh stages); and Mesa llvmpipe. Wave64 tests need 64-wide subgroups (AMD) or `LEONIDA_W64_EMULATE=1`. These are small test shaders: the game's own shaders are checked by `spirv-val` and by driver pipeline creation (`vk_pipeline_check`), not by their output | | Models (OBJ with real names, UVs, material references) | ✅ Exported. A ten-archive scan at decoder pin `e293917` recovered **382,781 models** with zero readback decode failures. This includes **343,327** models from `levels.rpf`. A full OBJ export of that archive is pending. See [recount and export scope](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). | | Texture dictionaries and world texture pools (DDS) | ✅ Exported. `rpf9dump` decodes BCPack BC1, BC3, BC4 and BC5 chunks in strict mode and skips BC6H, BC7 and chunks that need unconfirmed history; the assets stage then completes what it can with a clean-room decoder (`tools/bcpack.py`, which `tools/ttpf_assets.py` runs through `tools/ttpf_mips.py`) that rebuilds BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7, and records the rest as a `BCPackLimitation` in `manifest.json` (most BC6H/BC7 chunks and the unconfirmed-history ones need a local history table, which the repo does not ship) ([notes](docs/textures.md)) | | Audio banks (AWC: Opus, XMA2) | ✅ Exported whole. Opus repackaged **losslessly** as Ogg Opus; PCM (codec 0/2) as WAV; XMA2 decoded with ffmpeg. `--wav` adds 16-bit PCM WAV ([notes](docs/audio.md)) | | Music/radio config | ? Measured. **1,589** audio-config records with exact durations and AWC stream ids; station grouping and content-id lists; no per-track start offsets ([notes](docs/audio_config.md)) | | PE loader and import shims | ⚠️ Runs a stand-in executable end to end (`gta6rt --run`: CRT startup, statics, heap, files, threads, GDK imports through the shims, exit code back). Controllers through a GameInput shim on SDL3 (any controller SDL supports, rumble, DualSense trigger effects and lightbar; built when SDL3 is installed or with `-DLEONIDA_SDL3_FETCH=ON`, [notes](docs/gameinput.md)). `--trace-d3d12` logs every D3D12 call and its outcome for the first boot. Untested against the real executable | | Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan | ⚠️ In progress. A Vulkan-backed device behind the Xbox-ABI proxy creates queues, command lists, fences, descriptor heaps, committed, placed and reserved resources, render-target and depth views (3D targets included), texture views and samplers (2D, cube, 1D and 3D views, the depth and stencil planes of depth-stencil textures, packed formats such as B5G6R5, B4G4R4A4 and R9G9B9E5, buffer SRVs — raw, structured and typed; they go into the bindless set), root signatures, pipelines and query heaps, and draws run on Vulkan. Barriers, clears, uploads, copies (BC included), colour resolves, predication, CPU-side texture reads and writes, and occlusion, timestamp and pipeline-statistics queries run on Vulkan, checked on one GPU. The console-shaped command-list proxy, the measured `PresentX` queue slots (30/32, layout-detected) wired to the presentation core, and `AllocateUploadMemory` (list slot 148, a mapped-upload arena whose addresses translate to buffer device addresses in root descriptors and IA/SO views) cover the console-ABI surface the package measures. Still open: the console list tail and the descriptor-table record model ([plan](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)) | | Ray tracing (BVH) | ⚠️ In progress. `BuildRaytracingAccelerationStructure` builds BLASes and TLASes on the GPU in the console's XDXR BVH4 layout (the default; `LEONIDA_RT_AS=khr` uses Vulkan's own acceleration structures instead), which the translated shaders walk themselves through `image_bvh_intersect_ray` (all four triangle node types, TRI0-TRI3, with the barycentric remap byte); the GPU builder writes TRI0 and TRI1 leaves. Updates refit instead of rebuilding, and clone, compaction and the compacted/current postbuild sizes work; checked against a CPU reference on synthetic scenes. The build descriptions are recovered from the package's `XboxBvhBuilder.dll` ([notes](docs/xdxr.md)). The game's `*_bvh4.rpf` packs are measured: offline-built, dehydrated BLASes that rehydrate through that DLL with their geometry from the drawables in `levels.rpf` (measured on 8 of the 10 sampled BLAS; [notes](docs/bvh.md)). Not done in the builder: serialization. TRI1 pairing (no memory saved yet) and BOX16 nodes for `MINIMIZE_MEMORY` BLASes (an assumed switch) are in ([notes](docs/bvh.md)). Open: whether the game rehydrates the packs or rebuilds them ([#313](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/313)) | The table above is written by hand. To measure it on your own checkout (unit and runtime tests, which rows of the translator contract were confirmed on a GPU, measured imports, your corpus counts and, with `--github`, CI and the `D3D-` items), run `python -I tools/progress_dashboard.py --out ` and open `progress.html` ([notes](docs/progress_dashboard.md)). ## Platforms Nothing is playable on any platform yet (see *Project status*). What runs where today: | Platform | Today | |---|---| | Windows | Everything: `make_game.py`, the tools, and the runtime (`gta6rt` and the D3D12 → Vulkan layer) with its tests. | | Linux | The translator, the asset tools and the Vulkan GPU test tools build and run natively (tested on RADV and NVIDIA). The runtime is Windows code: it cross-compiles with clang-cl and xwin, and its tests run under Wine or Proton (*The Windows runtime on Linux, under Wine or Proton* below). The game is meant to run the same way, under Wine or Proton with the D3D12 layer on native Vulkan (#217). | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | The Python tools and the Vulkan test tools run natively, on MoltenVK (Homebrew) or KosmicKrisp. The runtime is Windows code and runs as on Linux, under Wine: CrossOver, arm64 with FEX or x86-64 under Rosetta (#1706, #1707, #1924; #3119 fixes the last loader tests there). Known gaps: no geometry stage and no `VK_EXT_mesh_shader` (those tests are skipped), 32-wide subgroups (wave64 shaders run emulated), and MoltenVK's float handling (`PerVertexKHR`, NaN compares, -0, the cost of `NoContraction`); [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) lists each (#2947). | | AMD RDNA1 (RX 5000) | A supported target: close to the console's RDNA2, and its 64-wide subgroups run the wave64 shaders natively. RX 5700 XT results pass the GPU test suite (#146); on RADV, pixel shaders without fragment barycentrics have a known difference (*Known problems* in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)) (#330). | GPU results from every platform are collected in #166; how to run the tests is in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). ## How to build The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy. **The easy way:** 1. Install the prerequisites below. 2. Download this project **with its submodule**: `git clone --recursive https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida`. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out `third_party/rpf9-explorer`. The build fetches it if `git` is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do. 3. Double-click **`Build.bat`**. It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to `Documents\Leonida`. A stopped build continues where it left off. Your game folder is the one that holds `MicrosoftGame.Config` and the `.rpf` archives, as plain files. **Prerequisites:** - **Your own copy** of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1. - **Windows 10/11 x64**, with about **400 GB** free for work files (an assets export alone measured about 337 GB before its audio step, in about 2 h 35 min). Disk sizes here are as Windows Explorer shows them, which are GiB: 400 GiB is about 430 GB in decimal units. They can go on another drive with `--work`. - [Python 3.12+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (tick "Add python.exe to PATH"). - [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0). - [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/), for `spirv-as` / `spirv-val`. - [LLVM 21+](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases) with the **AMDGPU target** for `llvm-mc`. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, `scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1` builds a native `llvm-mc.exe` with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets `LLVM_MC`; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use [conda](https://docs.conda.io/): `conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools` (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) used version 23.1.6), then set `LLVM_MC` to the full path of the `llvm-mc.exe` it installs (`where.exe llvm-mc` shows it once the environment is active; in PowerShell a bare `where` is `Where-Object`). Or install `llvm-21` in WSL and set `LLVM_MC` to the whole command, `LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc"` (see [docs/design.md](docs/design.md#disassembling-shaders)). On Linux, `llvm-mc` on PATH is enough. - Visual Studio 2022 with **Desktop development with C++** and the **Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer**, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare). - [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for `--wav`). **Is this PC strong enough?** [Can I Run Leonida](https://assttro.github.io/can-i-run-leonida/) is a lightweight browser-based checker that compares your PC against reference profiles. It's a rough estimate, not a benchmark. **Low disk space:** the ~400 GB figure is for the full build. To *run* the port, `--stages check,shaders,runtime` needs about 30 GB; the `assets` stage (~370 GB) is only for the asset tools, and `--wav` adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). `--work` and `--out` can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs `gta6rt --overlay `; `--overlay` is a `gta6rt` option, not a `make_game.py` one. Leave the `.s` files in `work/shaders/dxbc/disasm` in place: the next run checks them against the list in `disasm.done` and disassembles the missing ones again (all of them for a folder whose `disasm.done` predates that list), then translates every shader again. A `disasm` folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it. **From a terminal**, with the same behaviour and more control: ```powershell python -I make_game.py --find # list the copies found on this PC python -I make_game.py --pick # choose the game folder in a folder dialog python -I make_game.py --check # check your copy, build nothing python -I make_game.py --check --full-check # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow) python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work" python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets # only some stages python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large) python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off # auto (default), on or off; see below ``` `--wave64-emulate` decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, `auto`, asks `vulkaninfo` (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With `--mesh-compute`, only compute subgroup support is needed. On AMD's Windows driver, `auto` uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or `vulkaninfo` is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support. The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. `auto` can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use `--wave64-emulate on` to force emulation or `--wave64-emulate off` to force native wave64. Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: `--no-float-controls` (drop `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve`, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without `shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32`; needs PR #664's translator flag), `--bary-fallback` (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`), `--texel-offset-fallback` (fold `image_sample*_o` offsets into the coordinate, for devices without `VK_KHR_maintenance8`) and `--mesh-compute` (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`; on by itself on Intel's Windows Vulkan driver, whose native mesh draws crash, BUILD-2202, unless `--native-mesh`). Each is documented in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs. The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information. The build also records which decoder (the `third_party/rpf9-explorer` commit and the `tools/rpf9dump` sources) exported each archive's models and textures and each texture pool. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models, textures and pools are exported once more after upgrading. Stages: `check` always runs first; then `shaders`, `assets` and `runtime` run together when selected (they do not depend on each other). `pipelines` starts once the translated shaders are ready and, when this run includes runtime, that stage has finished rebuilding `vk_pipeline_check`, so it can overlap the rest of assets; it creates every translated shader on your GPU driver, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to `pipeline_cache.bin` in `--out` (the runtime doesn't load that cache yet, so it doesn't speed up the first boot). The shader translation is the longest CPU step: it runs on `--jobs` processes (half the CPU threads by default). When shaders and assets share the machine, that budget is split between them and passed to `rpf9dump` as `--jobs`; a solo assets run still lets `rpf9dump` use every core. Progress lines include percent and a rough ETA for translation shards, asset steps, and overall stage completion. On an interactive terminal, a LEONIDA setup screen lets you set jobs and whether stages overlap, then a key-switchable per-stage log view (`1`–`4` / `Tab`) keeps parallel output demuxed; full stage logs go under `work/logs/`. Use `--no-tui` (or redirect stdout) for the plain console. `--wav` is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to `work\assets\audio\wav` after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes. ### Vulkan diagnostics on Linux With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed: ```sh cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel ./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv ``` Pass the directory containing `index.json` and the translated SPIR-V files to `vk_pipeline_check`. `make_game.py` runs on Linux too. The `pipelines` stage uses the `vk_pipeline_check` built above (`runtime/build/linux`, or `runtime/build`), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing. ### Running the loader on Linux The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every push to `main` that changes `runtime/`, and on demand from the Actions tab (the `wine` job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the `runtime` stage cross-builds it into `runtime/build/windows` with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#known-problems); plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as `clang-cl-21`) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin) lays out, in `XWIN_DIR` or `~/.local/share/xwin-sdk` ([docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#the-windows-runtime-on-linux-under-wine-or-proton) has the one-time `xwin` command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the `runtime-windows` artifact of that workflow's `windows` job, unzipped: ```sh python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows ``` Either way it copies `gta6rt.exe` and `gta6rt_tls_host.dll` into `--out` and writes `gta6rt.sh` next to them, which starts `gta6rt.exe` with `wine`, or with the Wine named by `WINE` (for Proton, its `files/bin/wine`). The same option skips the build on Windows. On Linux, run `/gta6rt.sh --dry-run` to inspect the packaged title's imports, then `/gta6rt.sh --init` to check TLS callbacks and DLL initialization. Use `/gta6rt.sh --run` for startup. These commands use the package in `game_path.txt`, the port's `overlay` for writes, and Vulkan by default. When the Vulkan backend is selected with `LEONIDA_D3D12=vulkan`, the packaged runtime finds the translated shaders in `/shaders/spirv` using `shader_path.txt` beside `gta6rt.exe`. Set `LEONIDA_SHADERS` to use another directory. ## How it works | Piece | What it does | Where | |---|---|---| | Version check | Every package file's name, size and SHA-256 for each supported version | `game/`, `make_game.py` | | Shader pipeline | Carves DXBC containers from `shaders.rpf` without its encrypted table of contents. Unpacks the `XBCH` → `FSSM` native RDNA2 program, disassembles it with LLVM (`gfx1013`) and translates it to SPIR-V | `tools/shader_carve.py` ([optional Rust scanner](tools/shader_carve_native/README.md)), `fssm_unpack.py`, `shader_disasm.py`, `rdna2spirv.py` | | Asset export | Finds validated resources inside RPF9 archives and the loose `.ttpf` texture pools | `tools/rpf9dump` (on rpf9-explorer's Core) | | Runtime | Maps the PE image, resolves imports to shims (GDK, XMem, `d3d12_xs`) | `runtime/` | | Research tools | PE/RTTI inspection, raw carving, texture tiling probes, GPU test harnesses | `tools/`, `runtime/test/` | | Progress dashboard | One offline page of what passes, what changed since it last passed and what blocks next, built from test results and the docs' own tables; nothing is written inside the repo | `tools/progress_dashboard.py` | The translator's runtime contract (user SGPRs, push constants, memory model, bindless images, vertex fetch, system values) and all the format notes are in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md); the format, asset, runtime and validation notes are indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). The Xbox D3D12 plan is in [docs/d3d12_vulkan.md](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md). Audio bank formats and the export tools are in [docs/audio.md](docs/audio.md); [docs/related_projects.md](docs/related_projects.md) records the prior art we may read and the licence limits on it. ## Want to help? The biggest open pieces: - **Shader translator on hardware**: compute, mesh and geometry now translate (see the translator contract in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)); still open are the vertex-shader input layout (`v0` = `VertexIndex` is unverified if the console runs VS as NGG) and wave64 cross-half code in VS/PS/GS on 32-wide subgroups. - **Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan**: mesh-shader draws, indirect draw state and stream output are still open; #313 tracks the remaining method surface, and nothing has been checked against the real executable yet ([plan and status](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)). - **Model recovery**: investigate the 71 unrecovered fragment candidates in [`levels.rpf`](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Never attach game files, extracted assets or generated shaders to issues or pull requests. ## Credits - [rpf9-explorer](https://github.com/breadbbbb/rpf9-explorer) by breadbbbb: the RPF9 model, texture-pool and AWC decoders used by `tools/rpf9dump` (git submodule). - [Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa) (MIT): GFX10 resource-descriptor layout (`tools/gfx10_formats.json`), and the ACO/RADV rules used as reference for 16-bit results and shader system registers. - [libHttpClient](https://github.com/microsoft/libHttpClient) (MIT) by Microsoft: the XTaskQueue/XAsync implementation in `third_party/xtaskqueue`, used by the offline `xgameruntime` shim. - [LLVM](https://llvm.org/): AMDGPU disassembler. - Logo: ["Grand Theft Auto VI" icon by SlyDevil](https://www.steamgriddb.com/icon/122618) on SteamGridDB. - [SPIRV-Tools](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Tools): assembly and validation. Grand Theft Auto and all related names are trademarks of their owners. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by them. ## License GPLv3 (or any later version). See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
