items.readme:
Leonida

Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. Discord: https://discord.gg/xsqS3DqqVF Custom Git Mirror: https://git.notrexed.dev/notrexed/Leonida
## Project status **Early. The game does not boot yet.** Everything that can be done without the game's executable is in place, so work on booting can start as soon as one is available to a developer. | What | Status | |---|---| | Booting, story mode, anything playable | ❌ No | | Finding and checking your copy (Xbox Series 1.0.2.1) | ✅ Works | | Shaders: carve, unpack native RDNA2 code, disassemble | ✅ All 26,503 | | Shaders: RDNA2 → SPIR-V translation | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 translated**: 2,236 VS, 12,101 PS, 2,689 CS, 9,282 mesh, 195 geometry, with a per-shader metadata index for pipeline creation. The LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and the LLVM 23.1.3 Windows rerun at `43d0015` both translated all 26,503 ([Linux](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [Windows](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7074299915)). Translation and SPIR-V validation are separate steps; validation results are listed below. ⚠️ 23,841 are wave64: exact on 64-wide subgroups (AMD). On 32-wide subgroups (NVIDIA, Intel), compute and mesh shaders are exact with wave64 emulation (`--wave64-emulate`, on by default there); cross-half wave ops in vertex, pixel and geometry shaders are still approximate | | SPIR-V validation (`spirv-val`) | ✅ **26,503 / 26,503 passed** in the LLVM 23.1.5 Linux rerun at `c432cdc` and in the full-corpus rerun at `43d4703`, after `dcd8ecf` fixed the SPIR-V ID-bound error ([Linux rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/644#issuecomment-7072972586), [full-corpus rerun](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/881#issuecomment-7075507328)). On Windows at `43d0015`, all 26,503 translated but 26,501 passed validation; the two ID-bound failures were fixed by `dcd8ecf`. The intermediate `dedd75c` run also passed 26,501. | | Shader translator checked on a real GPU | ⚠️ The hand-written GPU tests (vertex fetch, texture sampling, exports, ALU ops, partial-register ops, barycentrics, wave-uniform branches, compute LDS/barriers/buffer stores, wave64 masks) have been run on more than 30 GPU and driver combinations, with results in [#166](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/166): NVIDIA Turing, Ampere, Ada and Blackwell (Windows and Linux); AMD GCN3, RDNA1, RDNA2, RDNA3 and RDNA4 (Windows driver and RADV); Intel Gen9 (ANV); Apple M1 (MoltenVK, no geometry or mesh stages); and Mesa llvmpipe. Wave64 tests need 64-wide subgroups (AMD) or `LEONIDA_W64_EMULATE=1`. These are small test shaders: the game's own shaders are checked by `spirv-val` and by driver pipeline creation (`vk_pipeline_check`), not by their output | | Models (OBJ with real names, UVs, material references) | ✅ Exported. A ten-archive scan at decoder pin `e293917` recovered **382,781 models** with zero readback decode failures. This includes **343,327** models from `levels.rpf`. A full OBJ export of that archive is pending. See [recount and export scope](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). | | Texture dictionaries and world texture pools (DDS) | ✅ Exported. `rpf9dump` decodes BCPack BC1, BC3, BC4 and BC5 chunks in strict mode and skips BC6H, BC7 and chunks that need unconfirmed history; the assets stage then completes what it can with a clean-room decoder (`tools/bcpack.py`, which `tools/ttpf_assets.py` runs through `tools/ttpf_mips.py`) that rebuilds BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7, and records the rest as a `BCPackLimitation` in `manifest.json` (most BC6H/BC7 chunks and the unconfirmed-history ones need a local history table, which the repo does not ship) ([notes](docs/textures.md)) | | Audio banks (AWC: Opus, XMA2) | ✅ Exported whole. Opus repackaged **losslessly** as Ogg Opus; PCM (codec 0/2) as WAV; XMA2 decoded with ffmpeg. `--wav` adds 16-bit PCM WAV ([notes](docs/audio.md)) | | Music/radio config | ? Measured. **1,589** audio-config records with exact durations and AWC stream ids; station grouping and content-id lists; no per-track start offsets ([notes](docs/audio_config.md)) | | PE loader and import shims | ⚠️ Runs a stand-in executable end to end (`gta6rt --run`: CRT startup, statics, heap, files, threads, GDK imports through the shims, exit code back). Controllers through a GameInput shim on SDL3 (any controller SDL supports, rumble, DualSense trigger effects and lightbar; built when SDL3 is installed or with `-DLEONIDA_SDL3_FETCH=ON`, [notes](docs/gameinput.md)). `--trace-d3d12` logs every D3D12 call and its outcome for the first boot. Untested against the real executable | | Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan | ⚠️ In progress. A Vulkan-backed device behind the Xbox-ABI proxy creates queues, command lists, fences, descriptor heaps, committed, placed and reserved resources, render-target and depth views (3D targets included), texture views and samplers (2D, cube, 1D and 3D views, the depth and stencil planes of depth-stencil textures, packed formats such as B5G6R5, B4G4R4A4 and R9G9B9E5, buffer SRVs — raw, structured and typed; they go into the bindless set), root signatures, pipelines and query heaps, and draws run on Vulkan. Barriers, clears, uploads, copies (BC included), colour resolves, predication, CPU-side texture reads and writes, and occlusion, timestamp and pipeline-statistics queries run on Vulkan, checked on one GPU. The console-shaped command-list proxy, the measured `PresentX` queue slots (30/32, layout-detected) wired to the presentation core, and `AllocateUploadMemory` (list slot 148, a mapped-upload arena whose addresses translate to buffer device addresses in root descriptors and IA/SO views) cover the console-ABI surface the package measures. Still open: the console list tail and the descriptor-table record model ([plan](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)) | | Ray tracing (BVH) | ⚠️ In progress. `BuildRaytracingAccelerationStructure` builds BLASes and TLASes on the GPU in the console's XDXR BVH4 layout (the default; `LEONIDA_RT_AS=khr` uses Vulkan's own acceleration structures instead), which the translated shaders walk themselves through `image_bvh_intersect_ray` (all four triangle node types, TRI0-TRI3, with the barycentric remap byte); the GPU builder writes TRI0 and TRI1 leaves. Updates refit instead of rebuilding, and clone, compaction and the compacted/current postbuild sizes work; checked against a CPU reference on synthetic scenes. The build descriptions are recovered from the package's `XboxBvhBuilder.dll` ([notes](docs/xdxr.md)). The game's `*_bvh4.rpf` packs are measured: offline-built, dehydrated BLASes that rehydrate through that DLL with their geometry from the drawables in `levels.rpf` (measured on 8 of the 10 sampled BLAS; [notes](docs/bvh.md)). Not done in the builder: serialization. TRI1 pairing (no memory saved yet) and BOX16 nodes for `MINIMIZE_MEMORY` BLASes (an assumed switch) are in ([notes](docs/bvh.md)). Open: whether the game rehydrates the packs or rebuilds them ([#313](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/313)) | The table above is written by hand. To measure it on your own checkout (unit and runtime tests, which rows of the translator contract were confirmed on a GPU, measured imports, your corpus counts and, with `--github`, CI and the `D3D-` items), run `python -I tools/progress_dashboard.py --out ` and open `progress.html` ([notes](docs/progress_dashboard.md)). ## Platforms Nothing is playable on any platform yet (see *Project status*). What runs where today: | Platform | Today | |---|---| | Windows | Everything: `make_game.py`, the tools, and the runtime (`gta6rt` and the D3D12 → Vulkan layer) with its tests. | | Linux | The translator, the asset tools and the Vulkan GPU test tools build and run natively (tested on RADV and NVIDIA). The runtime is Windows code: it cross-compiles with clang-cl and xwin, and its tests run under Wine or Proton (*The Windows runtime on Linux, under Wine or Proton* below). The game is meant to run the same way, under Wine or Proton with the D3D12 layer on native Vulkan (#217). | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | The Python tools and the Vulkan test tools run natively, on MoltenVK (Homebrew) or KosmicKrisp. The runtime is Windows code and runs as on Linux, under Wine: CrossOver, arm64 with FEX or x86-64 under Rosetta (#1706, #1707, #1924; #3119 fixes the last loader tests there). Known gaps: no geometry stage and no `VK_EXT_mesh_shader` (those tests are skipped), 32-wide subgroups (wave64 shaders run emulated), and MoltenVK's float handling (`PerVertexKHR`, NaN compares, -0, the cost of `NoContraction`); [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) lists each (#2947). | | AMD RDNA1 (RX 5000) | A supported target: close to the console's RDNA2, and its 64-wide subgroups run the wave64 shaders natively. RX 5700 XT results pass the GPU test suite (#146); on RADV, pixel shaders without fragment barycentrics have a known difference (*Known problems* in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)) (#330). | GPU results from every platform are collected in #166; how to run the tests is in [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). ## How to build The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy. **The easy way:** 1. Install the prerequisites below. 2. Download this project **with its submodule**: `git clone --recursive https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida`. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out `third_party/rpf9-explorer`. The build fetches it if `git` is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do. 3. Double-click **`Build.bat`**. It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to `Documents\Leonida`. A stopped build continues where it left off. Your game folder is the one that holds `MicrosoftGame.Config` and the `.rpf` archives, as plain files. **Prerequisites:** - **Your own copy** of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1. - **Windows 10/11 x64**, with about **400 GB** free for work files (an assets export alone measured about 337 GB before its audio step, in about 2 h 35 min). Disk sizes here are as Windows Explorer shows them, which are GiB: 400 GiB is about 430 GB in decimal units. They can go on another drive with `--work`. - [Python 3.12+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (tick "Add python.exe to PATH"). - [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0). - [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/), for `spirv-as` / `spirv-val`. - [LLVM 21+](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases) with the **AMDGPU target** for `llvm-mc`. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, `scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1` builds a native `llvm-mc.exe` with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets `LLVM_MC`; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use [conda](https://docs.conda.io/): `conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools` (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) used version 23.1.6), then set `LLVM_MC` to the full path of the `llvm-mc.exe` it installs (`where.exe llvm-mc` shows it once the environment is active; in PowerShell a bare `where` is `Where-Object`). Or install `llvm-21` in WSL and set `LLVM_MC` to the whole command, `LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc"` (see [docs/design.md](docs/design.md#disassembling-shaders)). On Linux, `llvm-mc` on PATH is enough. - Visual Studio 2022 with **Desktop development with C++** and the **Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer**, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare). - [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for `--wav`). **Is this PC strong enough?** [Can I Run Leonida](https://assttro.github.io/can-i-run-leonida/) is a lightweight browser-based checker that compares your PC against reference profiles. It's a rough estimate, not a benchmark. **Low disk space:** the ~400 GB figure is for the full build. To *run* the port, `--stages check,shaders,runtime` needs about 30 GB; the `assets` stage (~370 GB) is only for the asset tools, and `--wav` adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). `--work` and `--out` can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs `gta6rt --overlay `; `--overlay` is a `gta6rt` option, not a `make_game.py` one. Leave the `.s` files in `work/shaders/dxbc/disasm` in place: the next run checks them against the list in `disasm.done` and disassembles the missing ones again (all of them for a folder whose `disasm.done` predates that list), then translates every shader again. A `disasm` folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it. **From a terminal**, with the same behaviour and more control: ```powershell python -I make_game.py --find # list the copies found on this PC python -I make_game.py --pick # choose the game folder in a folder dialog python -I make_game.py --check # check your copy, build nothing python -I make_game.py --check --full-check # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow) python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work" python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets # only some stages python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large) python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off # auto (default), on or off; see below ``` `--wave64-emulate` decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, `auto`, asks `vulkaninfo` (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With `--mesh-compute`, only compute subgroup support is needed. On AMD's Windows driver, `auto` uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or `vulkaninfo` is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support. The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. `auto` can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use `--wave64-emulate on` to force emulation or `--wave64-emulate off` to force native wave64. Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: `--no-float-controls` (drop `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve`, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without `shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32`; needs PR #664's translator flag), `--bary-fallback` (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`), `--texel-offset-fallback` (fold `image_sample*_o` offsets into the coordinate, for devices without `VK_KHR_maintenance8`) and `--mesh-compute` (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`; on by itself on Intel's Windows Vulkan driver, whose native mesh draws crash, BUILD-2202, unless `--native-mesh`). Each is documented in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs. The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information. The build also records which decoder (the `third_party/rpf9-explorer` commit and the `tools/rpf9dump` sources) exported each archive's models and textures and each texture pool. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models, textures and pools are exported once more after upgrading. Stages: `check` always runs first; then `shaders`, `assets` and `runtime` run together when selected (they do not depend on each other). `pipelines` starts once the translated shaders are ready and, when this run includes runtime, that stage has finished rebuilding `vk_pipeline_check`, so it can overlap the rest of assets; it creates every translated shader on your GPU driver, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to `pipeline_cache.bin` in `--out` (the runtime doesn't load that cache yet, so it doesn't speed up the first boot). The shader translation is the longest CPU step: it runs on `--jobs` processes (half the CPU threads by default). When shaders and assets share the machine, that budget is split between them and passed to `rpf9dump` as `--jobs`; a solo assets run still lets `rpf9dump` use every core. Progress lines include percent and a rough ETA for translation shards, asset steps, and overall stage completion. On an interactive terminal, a LEONIDA setup screen lets you set jobs and whether stages overlap, then a key-switchable per-stage log view (`1`–`4` / `Tab`) keeps parallel output demuxed; full stage logs go under `work/logs/`. Use `--no-tui` (or redirect stdout) for the plain console. `--wav` is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to `work\assets\audio\wav` after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes. ### Vulkan diagnostics on Linux With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed: ```sh cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel ./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv ``` Pass the directory containing `index.json` and the translated SPIR-V files to `vk_pipeline_check`. `make_game.py` runs on Linux too. The `pipelines` stage uses the `vk_pipeline_check` built above (`runtime/build/linux`, or `runtime/build`), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing. ### Running the loader on Linux The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every push to `main` that changes `runtime/`, and on demand from the Actions tab (the `wine` job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the `runtime` stage cross-builds it into `runtime/build/windows` with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#known-problems); plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as `clang-cl-21`) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin) lays out, in `XWIN_DIR` or `~/.local/share/xwin-sdk` ([docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#the-windows-runtime-on-linux-under-wine-or-proton) has the one-time `xwin` command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the `runtime-windows` artifact of that workflow's `windows` job, unzipped: ```sh python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows ``` Either way it copies `gta6rt.exe` and `gta6rt_tls_host.dll` into `--out` and writes `gta6rt.sh` next to them, which starts `gta6rt.exe` with `wine`, or with the Wine named by `WINE` (for Proton, its `files/bin/wine`). The same option skips the build on Windows. On Linux, run `/gta6rt.sh --dry-run` to inspect the packaged title's imports, then `/gta6rt.sh --init` to check TLS callbacks and DLL initialization. Use `/gta6rt.sh --run` for startup. These commands use the package in `game_path.txt`, the port's `overlay` for writes, and Vulkan by default. When the Vulkan backend is selected with `LEONIDA_D3D12=vulkan`, the packaged runtime finds the translated shaders in `/shaders/spirv` using `shader_path.txt` beside `gta6rt.exe`. Set `LEONIDA_SHADERS` to use another directory. ## How it works | Piece | What it does | Where | |---|---|---| | Version check | Every package file's name, size and SHA-256 for each supported version | `game/`, `make_game.py` | | Shader pipeline | Carves DXBC containers from `shaders.rpf` without its encrypted table of contents. Unpacks the `XBCH` → `FSSM` native RDNA2 program, disassembles it with LLVM (`gfx1013`) and translates it to SPIR-V | `tools/shader_carve.py` ([optional Rust scanner](tools/shader_carve_native/README.md)), `fssm_unpack.py`, `shader_disasm.py`, `rdna2spirv.py` | | Asset export | Finds validated resources inside RPF9 archives and the loose `.ttpf` texture pools | `tools/rpf9dump` (on rpf9-explorer's Core) | | Runtime | Maps the PE image, resolves imports to shims (GDK, XMem, `d3d12_xs`) | `runtime/` | | Research tools | PE/RTTI inspection, raw carving, texture tiling probes, GPU test harnesses | `tools/`, `runtime/test/` | | Progress dashboard | One offline page of what passes, what changed since it last passed and what blocks next, built from test results and the docs' own tables; nothing is written inside the repo | `tools/progress_dashboard.py` | The translator's runtime contract (user SGPRs, push constants, memory model, bindless images, vertex fetch, system values) and all the format notes are in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md); the format, asset, runtime and validation notes are indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). The Xbox D3D12 plan is in [docs/d3d12_vulkan.md](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md). Audio bank formats and the export tools are in [docs/audio.md](docs/audio.md); [docs/related_projects.md](docs/related_projects.md) records the prior art we may read and the licence limits on it. ## Want to help? The biggest open pieces: - **Shader translator on hardware**: compute, mesh and geometry now translate (see the translator contract in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)); still open are the vertex-shader input layout (`v0` = `VertexIndex` is unverified if the console runs VS as NGG) and wave64 cross-half code in VS/PS/GS on 32-wide subgroups. - **Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan**: mesh-shader draws, indirect draw state and stream output are still open; #313 tracks the remaining method surface, and nothing has been checked against the real executable yet ([plan and status](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)). - **Model recovery**: investigate the 71 unrecovered fragment candidates in [`levels.rpf`](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Never attach game files, extracted assets or generated shaders to issues or pull requests. ## Credits - [rpf9-explorer](https://github.com/breadbbbb/rpf9-explorer) by breadbbbb: the RPF9 model, texture-pool and AWC decoders used by `tools/rpf9dump` (git submodule). - [Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa) (MIT): GFX10 resource-descriptor layout (`tools/gfx10_formats.json`), and the ACO/RADV rules used as reference for 16-bit results and shader system registers. - [libHttpClient](https://github.com/microsoft/libHttpClient) (MIT) by Microsoft: the XTaskQueue/XAsync implementation in `third_party/xtaskqueue`, used by the offline `xgameruntime` shim. - [LLVM](https://llvm.org/): AMDGPU disassembler. - Logo: ["Grand Theft Auto VI" icon by SlyDevil](https://www.steamgriddb.com/icon/122618) on SteamGridDB. - [SPIRV-Tools](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Tools): assembly and validation. # FORZERO: BUDGET · 有限竞速：地贫线

纯代码驱动的 WebGL 2 三维自行车与多载具竞速游戏。全部场景、建筑、植被、3D 车辆与动态骑行音效均由程序化代码生成。

玩家可在 **深圳大学 · 粤海校区（荔园环骑）**、**伦敦 Bloomsbury（UCL）** 与 **佛山顺德 · 顺峰山公园** 三张立体地图间自由骑行与站台旅行，挑战 20 条固定赛道、种子赛道与每周挑战。

---

## 核心特色

- **三大风格化开放地图与 20 条固定赛道**：
  - **深圳大学 · 粤海校区（荔园环骑）**：9 条赛道（含校园环线、图书馆穿行、双湖绿道、杜鹃山爬坡/下坡、荔香公园城景环线、白石科创城际冲刺等）及高风险切线近路。
  - **伦敦 Bloomsbury（UCL）**：7 条赛道（主庭院、双广场、医学区折返、圣潘克拉斯、商街与大英博物馆、学院穿堂等）。
  - **佛山顺德 · 顺峰山公园**：4 条赛道——青云湖环线（含九孔伏波桥与青云塔），以及「神步山爬坡赛」「神步山下坡赛」「顺峰山环山耐力赛」（湖山联动 1.95 km 闭环、3 条高风险窄切捷径、压实碎石独立物理、草地/水域/落崖强制遣返、环湖观光接驳车尾流与公园 10 地标闪送）。
- **120 Hz 物理与双姿态博弈**：
  - 支持自行车（5 槽深度改装：轮胎 / 齿比 / 刹车 / 车架几何 / 冲刺调校 + 4 套流派预设 + 程序化 3D 外观定制）、电动自行车、电动轮椅、越野小摩托。
  - 支持在设置中按局开启「车辆碰撞箱」（与动态车流/巡游车或联机骑手发生实体碰撞）。
  - 自行车根据速度、坡度、转向与冲刺自动切换 **伏身破风（Aero Tuck）** 与 **起身摇车（Out-of-Saddle Sprint）**，配合动态车流与联机尾流破风。
- **种子赛道 v2、每周挑战与地图风场**：
  - `S2-*` / `U2-*` 确定性随机生成合规赛道；每周挑战按本地周历锁定种子并绑定动态天气与风场；常规单人与联机房间也均支持自由调节地图风速（`0–15 m/s`）与 8 方位风向。
- **幽灵竞速、复盘单练与全勋章**：
  - `.ghost.json` 影子文件导出/导入、多影子同场群跑、实时滚动毫秒差、紫牌大师挑战（`0.90 × 金牌时间`）、俯视图走线对比与任意检查点区间「单练」。
- **局域网 P2P 好友联机**：
  - 基于 Node.js 内置 HTTP + SSE + WebRTC DataChannel，覆盖深大粤海、伦敦 UCL 与顺峰山公园三张地图，支持 BO1 / BO3 / 五轮积分联赛 / 盲盒随机 / 铁人三项，支持房主自定义赛前**改车时间（0–180s）**与**车辆碰撞箱**开关。
- **全代码 Web Audio 音效与多端自适应**：
  - 内置合成风噪、胎噪、棘轮声（可在设置中静音），支持 `sound/` 自定义音频替换；桌面多文件版与手机单文件离线版全触屏适配。

---

## 操作指南

| 按键 / 触屏 | 功能 |
| --- | --- |
| `W` `A` `S` `D` / 方向键 | 加速、转向、刹车 / 停车长按倒车 |
| `Shift` | 自行车冲刺（坡道或低速出弯触发起身摇车） |
| `M` | 打开 / 关闭俯视导览地图（支持「看赛道」与海拔剖面） |
| `R` | 开始 / 重新开始当前计时赛 |
| `P` | 暂停 / 继续 |
| `F` | 回归赛道（+2 秒罚时） |
| `B` / `H` | 摇车铃 |
| `Esc` | 打开 / 关闭设置与自行车工坊 |

---

## 本地运行方式

### 1. 桌面完整版（推荐，支持本地自动存档与好友联机）
- 打开 `forzero-budget-1.8.6/` 目录：
  - **Windows 一键启动**：双击 **`启动游戏.bat`**（自动启动本地应用壳并将存档同步至 `save/player-data.json`，关闭网页约 8 秒后后台自动退出；未安装 Node.js 时会自动降级打开 `index.html`）。
  - **直接浏览器游玩**：直接用现代浏览器打开 `forzero-budget-1.8.6/index.html`（支持 `file://` 离线单人游玩与导入/导出 JSON 备份）。
  - **常驻服务部署**（需要 Node.js 22+）：
    ```sh
    cd forzero-budget-1.8.6
    HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=8787 node server.mjs
    ```

### 2. 手机单文件离线版
- 将根目录的 `forzero-budget-mobile-1.8.6.html` 发送至手机，使用 Chrome / Edge / Safari 或系统浏览器打开即可离线游玩（支持竖屏与横屏触屏）。

### 3. 本地构建与自动化测试
```powershell
python szu-litchi-dev/ride-update/build.py
node --check szu-litchi-dev/ride-update/game.js
node --check szu-litchi-dev/online/server.mjs
node szu-litchi-dev/ride-update/verify-mountain.mjs
node szu-litchi-dev/ride-update/verify-park.mjs
node szu-litchi-dev/ride-update/verify-1.6.0.mjs --mountain
```

---

- 第三方依赖或运行环境工具（如 Node.js、浏览器等）遵循其各自原有许可协议。

# SeedSwap

SeedSwap lets you play Switch 1 games on a Switch 2 by running them in place of Seedsow Lullaby or
another installed Switch 1 game.
- It needs firmware 23.0.1 with kaiHEN.
- You pick and switch games on the console.

![SeedSwap's Library](images/library.png)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Switching to another game](images/switch-confirm.png) | ![Picking a host](images/hosts.png) |
| ![Converting a dump on the console](images/convert.png) | ![Choosing the play user](images/play-user.png) |
| ![Saves and backups](images/saves.png) | ![Setting up an installed game as a host](images/add-host.png) |

These screenshots come from SeedSwap 0.12.0's PC preview, which runs the real UI. The users and user
IDs in them are made up.

This repository builds two things:
- **The Seedsow save.** It holds alula's launcher, the seedsow-semi-untethered exploit chain, and
  SeedSwap's A/B launcher entries.
- **The SD card files.** These are SeedSwap itself, kaiHEN's loader stage, and the install image.

## Build

1. **Get SeedSwap (`seedswap.nro`).** GitHub Actions builds it from `seedswap/` on every push:
   - Download the `seedswap-nro` artifact of a run.
   - Or, when the repo has a `v*` tag, get it from that tag's release.
   - Or build it yourself (see `seedswap/README.md`).
2. **Build the rest** (needs Python 3.8 or newer):

       python3 build.py --nro seedswap.nro

   This writes:
   - `out/save/`: the Seedsow save;
   - `out/seedsow-seedswap-save.zip`: the same save as one zip;
   - `out/sd/`: the SD card files.

   It also downloads three parts at fixed commits and checks every file against `SHA256SUMS.txt`:
   - alula's launcher files;
   - the unchanged seedsow-semi-untethered modules;
   - kurumuz's ns2jb RO helper.

   The repository doesn't include these parts: alula's and kurumuz's repositories have no licence
   file, so `build.py` downloads all three from their sources.

The CI run does the same steps and checks the result. Its SeedSwap must match the tested build byte
for byte. It uploads only `seedswap.nro`.

## Install (firmware 23.0.1, kaiHEN on the SD card)

**[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) has the full step-by-step guide.** It also covers updating an existing
seedsow-semi-untethered save over the network (`upload_save.py`).

> **Use only your own games and keys.** Only play dumps of games you own, made yourself, and only use
> the `prod.keys` from your own console. This repository has no games or keys; don't download them
> from anywhere.

In short:

1. Copy `out/sd/` to the root of the SD card.
2. Put the save on a spare user's Seedsow save with ns2jb + ns2-savekit (back up, then replace from
   `out/save/`).
3. Restart. Start Seedsow on that user, and press A in the launcher.
4. Open SeedSwap. It finds the user with the exploit save and never uses that user.
5. In the Saves tab, press Y and pick the user who plays. Restart and run the launcher (A) again.
6. In the Library, press - and pick a host: Seedsow, or any installed Switch 1 game. Then switch games.

## Launcher buttons

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| A | Runs kaiHEN, with SeedSwap's loader first. |
| B | Same as A, with the newest seedsow-semi-untethered scan and wave stages (e5c14e5). Where e5c14e5 ends the run after an uneven race wave, B retries like A and logs it. Then B installs SeedSwap from the save to `SD:/switch`, unless the SD copy is the same or newer. |
| Y | alula's HTTP server (port 8080). |
| Hold - first | Runs the previous A or B. |

## What is here

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `upload_save.py` | Updates an existing seedsow-semi-untethered save over the launcher's HTTP server (see INSTALL.md). |
| `save/` | Our files for the Seedsow save: the kaiHEN stage that starts the loader (`s2_kh_ro.lua`), the A/B menu, the A and B entries, their hardened copies, and B's two newer modules. |
| `sd/` | The loader stage (`kaihen/s2_ml.lua`), `ml_image.lua`, `tpl.lua`, and the install image. The image has Seedsow plus 9 spare host slots. Its save guard is on nobody until you pick the play user. |
| `seedswap/` | SeedSwap's source. |
| `loader/` | Our changes to ns2jb-modloader, which the install image is built from, and the image tools. |
| `licenses/` | Licence texts. |

## Licences

- **GPL-2.0 (`LICENSE`):** everything in this repository except the third-party parts below:
  - `seedswap/`: SeedSwap's source, `GPL-2.0-only` in each file;
  - `save/`, `sd/` and `loader/`: these derive from seedsow-semi-untethered and
    SebaaMG/ns2jb-modloader, which are both GPL-2.0.
- **Third-party parts:**
  - seedsow-semi-untethered's CivSwitchFS part is MIT (`licenses/CivSwitchFS-MIT.txt`);
  - `seedswap/source/vendor/stb_image.h` is MIT or public domain;
  - `seedswap/source/font_data.c` and `seedswap/assets/fonts/` are the Ubuntu font
    (`licenses/UBUNTU-FONT-LICENCE.txt`).
- **Downloaded files:** these keep their authors' terms.

# GKMSMainWheel

学園アイドルマスター 的考试引擎与原生核心、培育模拟器、出牌网络。

Ver1.0 Morgendämmerung

| 目录 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `GakumasCLI/` | 考试引擎、C++ 原生核心 |
| `GKMSPS/` | 培育模拟器 |
| `GKMSUINet/` | 出牌网络 |

## 准备

Python 3.11 以上。仓库不含游戏数据，master 由 [vertesan/gakumasu-diff](https://github.com/vertesan/gakumasu-diff) 在本地生成。

```
pip install -r requirements.txt
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/vertesan/gakumasu-diff ../gakumasu-diff
python -B GakumasCLI/gkms.py master-bootstrap build --mirror ../gakumasu-diff
```

原生核心：

- Linux：`sh GakumasCLI/native/build.sh`
- Windows：在仓库根目录的 `gkms.local.cmd` 写入 `set "GKMS_VCVARS=<vcvars64.bat 的路径>"`，再运行 `GakumasCLI\native\build.cmd GakumasCLI\native\build`

GKMSUINet 的训练与导出另需 `torch`、`onnxruntime`。

## 使用

```
python -B -m GKMSPS.ps.cli play GKMSPS/examples/formation.json
python -B -m GKMSPS.ps.cli auto GKMSPS/examples/formation.json --engine
pip install pytest
python -m pytest -q tests
```

## 许可证

[AGPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE)

# GTA6 PC Port Archive

Archived copies of four open-source projects that worked on running GTA VI on PC, saved on 2026-11-23 and 2026-11-24.
ZERO of Rockstars game assets, files, or leaked info is on this repo, NOTHING HERE IS BREAKING ANY LAW OR ANYONE'S TOS
## Important links

- [portwatch-vi.xyz](https://portwatch-vi.xyz)
- [leonida.now](https://leonida.now)

| Folder | Project | Original | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`leonida/`](leonida) | Leonida: native PC recompilation of the Xbox version | `ItsNotRexed/Leonida` (removed from GitHub on 2026-11-23) | GPL-3.0 |
| [`xcl/`](xcl) | xcl: Xbox Series compatibility layer for Windows | `ivall/xcl` | GPL-2.0 |
| [`victory/`](victory) | VIctory: an attempt at running GTA VI on PC | `Marvisak/VIctory` | GPL-3.0 |
| [`xbox2windows/`](xbox2windows) | Xbox2Windows: static recompilation of Xbox Series software for x64 Windows | `R0Y00/Xbox2Windows` | MIT |
| [`github-export/`](github-export) | each project's issues, pull requests and comments | | |

Each project folder keeps its own license file. Leonida's `third_party/rpf9-explorer` submodule
(`breadbbbb/rpf9-explorer`) has no license, so it is not included.

## Branches

`main` is a single snapshot of all four projects. Each project's original history, with its original commits, authors,
hashes and file paths, is on its own branches:

| Project | Code | Pull requests | Issues and comments |
|---|---|---|---|
| Leonida | `leonida/main` | `leonida/pr/<number>` (9,425) | `leonida/github-export` |
| xcl | `xcl/main` | `xcl/pr/<number>` (361) | `xcl/github-export` |
| VIctory | `victory/main` | `victory/pr/<number>` (145) | `victory/github-export` |
| Xbox2Windows | `xbox2windows/main`, other branches as `xbox2windows/branch/<name>` (125), tag `xbox2windows/<tag>` | `xbox2windows/pr/<number>` (983) | `xbox2windows/github-export` |

Get one project on its own:

```sh
git clone --branch leonida/main --single-branch https://github.com/Guernica4u/GTA6-PC-Port-Archive.git leonida
```

## Issues and comments

`github-export/<project>/data/` holds gzipped JSON Lines straight from the GitHub API: one issue, pull request or
comment per line. Each folder's README lists the files and counts.
